titleEn: On a Slippery Path, One Step at a Time!

pages.text: "The rain stopped! Let's go to the well tree!" Mumu hopped off the porch. Rain had left the dirt road wet and shiny.
"My legs are fastest. I'll get there before Taro!" Mumu bounded ahead. Wet soil squelched underfoot.
Then a hind leg slid far forward. Mumu landed on their bottom with a thump. A long skid marked the wet soil.
Taro ran over and helped Mumu up. "Does it hurt? Wet soil is slippery." Mumu's ears drooped. "My legs keep sliding."
A lizard passed at their feet, placing one foot after another very slowly. It did not slip at all.
"Let's walk like the lizard," Taro said. "One, steps instead of bounds! Two, step on grassy places! Three, stop if it's slippery!" Mumu repeated, "On a Slippery Path, One Step at a Time!"
Mumu bent their long legs and stepped one foot at a time, avoiding shiny patches and choosing grass. Rustling replaced the squelching.
They reached the well tree without one slip. Mumu turned their ears and looked back. Only two side-by-side trails of footprints marked the path.
The next day, the path was wet again. Mumu called first, "One, a step at a time! Two, grassy places! Three, stop if it's slippery! On a Slippery Path, One Step at a Time!"
Taro held Mumu with both arms. "Slow is fine when we come together." On a wet path, careful feet were better than fast legs. Mumu stepped lightly. "On a Slippery Path, One Step at a Time!"
